what_its_for: Buspirone is used to treat anxiety disorders. It helps reduce feelings of nervousness, worry, tension, and irritability. It works differently than other anxiety medicines — it is not a sedative and is not habit-forming.
how_to_take: Take buspirone by mouth with or without food, but try to take it the same way every time (either always with food or always without food). Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. Do NOT drink grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can change how the drug works in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose, such as 7.5 mg twice a day. Your dose may be slowly increased every few days as needed. The typical dose is between 15 mg and 30 mg per day, split into 2 or 3 doses. Never take more than 60 mg per day unless your doctor tells you to. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store buspirone at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely through a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of buspirone in your blood and cause side effects. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking buspirone, as it may increase dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking buspirone with MAO inhibitors (such as phenelzine or tranylcypromine), as this can cause a dangerous reaction.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, severe dizziness or fainting, confusion or unusual changes in mood or behavior, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if your anxiety does not improve after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Buspirone does NOT work right away like some other anxiety medicines. It usually takes 2 to 4 weeks before you start feeling better, and sometimes up to 6 weeks for the full effect. Do not stop taking it just because you do not feel better right away. Keep taking it as directed and talk to your doctor if you have concerns.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as side effects like dizziness may be more likely, increasing the risk of falls. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using buspirone if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if buspirone passes into breast milk — ask your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be safe for you. Children: Buspirone is generally not recommended for children under 18 unless specifically prescribed by a doctor.
